tasks.short: Meet the student board to advise, review event and budget requests, answer board members' questions, and attend student events.

steps.what: Biology lecturer acts as adviser to the student organization's board in meetings
Student board fills the event and budget request form
Biology lecturer reviews the student organization's event and budget requests: pieced together from e-mails today, as one form with budget status and risk checklist after the change
Biology lecturer checks the final advice on the request: comments fit the plan, the remaining budget and the risk checklist
Biology lecturer sends the checked advice to the board in the workflow tool
Biology lecturer answers board members' questions about university rules by e-mail
Biology lecturer attends student organization events

tasks.design: Student organizations submit event and budget requests through a form in the university's workflow tool ({WORKFLOW}) that shows their remaining budget and attaches the event's risk checklist, so the adviser reviews one complete request instead of piecing it together from e-mails, checks the advice and sends it once. A handbook page answers common rule questions. Advising the board and attending events stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived by e-mail without budget status or checklists.
tasks.enabler_now: Workflow tools take request forms with budget status.
tasks.still_hard: Boards change every year and relearn the rules.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a new board handle its first conflict.
tasks.altitude: The adviser reviews complete requests; advising stays.

evidence.claim: Workflow tools can take request forms that show budget status.

assumptions: Boundary: from the board meeting to the event attended; university funding decisions are outside.
Input contract: request form set up; fallback is e-mail.
Boards fill the form in about the time an e-mail took; their time is shown in s1b. s2 keeps 50 for reading and judging each request; s3 keeps 70 for questions the handbook does not answer.
research_questions: Are requests complete on first submission more often?

incremental.description: Biology lecturer updates the handbook page.

approvals.approved_version: The adviser's comments on this event and budget request exactly as checked by the lecturer in s2b, sent once to the student board in the workflow tool; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: boards still send half of their requests by e-mail, so s2 keeps 75 (8.3); high: requests come by form as assumed (12.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet the client to define the question, review literature and data, write the advisory report, check it, send it to the client, and present findings.

steps.what: Biology lecturer meets the government or industry client to define the question
Biology lecturer reviews literature and data for professional consulting

loop.input: The client's question and the library's citation databases; no client documents.
loop.check: Each suggested title must resolve by DOI or catalogue, else it is dropped; the lecturer reads the sources used and checks that each supports the point it is cited for.
loop.stop: One search per question; if nothing resolves, the lecturer searches by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Client questions cross fields; keyword search misses related work.

steps.what: Biology lecturer writes the advisory report
Biology lecturer checks the final report: the advice follows from the evidence and answers the client's question, and sources are cited correctly
Biology lecturer sends the checked report to the client: by e-mail today, from the university's secure file share after the change
Biology lecturer presents findings to the client

tasks.design: A research search tool over the library's citation databases ({OTHER}) suggests related titles for the client's question; titles that do not resolve are dropped, and no client documents are uploaded. The report uses the university's advisory template with set sections. Once checked, the lecturer sends the report to the client from the university's secure file share. Defining the question, writing the advice and presenting stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Literature was searched by keyword and reports laid out from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Citation databases suggest related work; advisory templates are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Client data are often confidential and stay out of search tools.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a client the honest answer they did not want.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and layout; the advice stays.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI gives topic summaries and foundational papers.
Uploading a confidential document to generative AI breaches confidentiality under funder rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the consulting request to findings presented; contract terms are outside.
Input contract: library licences the databases; fallback is keyword search.
The lecturer checks every report before it is sent.
s2 keeps 70: suggestions replace some searching, but reading literature and data stays. s3 keeps 80 because the template gives only the set sections. s5 keeps 20 for sharing the file.
research_questions: Is literature review time per job shorter?

incremental.description: Biology lecturer keeps the advisory template current.

approvals.approved_version: The advisory report exactly as checked by the lecturer in s4, sent once to the named client contact from the secure file share; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the question is too narrow for suggestions to help, so s2 stays 100 (9.5); high: suggestions and template as assumed (17.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The biology lecturer keeps advising students and clients; e-mailed requests, keyword searches and report layout shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer with more time for advice.
